lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Πτολεμαῖον παρανατέλλει ὁ τράχηλος τοῦ μεγάλου ἄρκτου
lines.en: And according to Ptolemy there co-rises the neck of the Great Bear

lines.text: καὶ ἡ ἀριστερὰ αὐτοῦ χεὶρ καὶ αἱ χεῖρες τοῦ Λέοντος καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ
lines.en: and its left hand and the hands of Leo and the half of the

lines.text: πλοίου.
lines.en: Ship.

lines.text: Τῷ δὲ βʹ δεκανῷ τοῦ Λέοντος παρανατέλλει παῖς ἄνω ἔχων τὴν
lines.en: And with the 2nd decan of Leo there co-rises a boy holding up his

lines.text: χεῖρα καὶ μεγάλα φωνῶν καὶ πέντε ἔχων παρ’ αὑτοῦ σείστρας καὶ
lines.en: hand and shouting loudly and having beside him five sistra and

lines.text: ὀρχηστὴν καὶ τραγούδια διάφορα· παρανατέλλει δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ ποτήριον
lines.en: a dancer and various songs; and there co-rises with him also a cup

lines.text: οἴνου καὶ ζαμάρα καὶ κέρατα γαζελίου δορκάδος καὶ νῆσσα καὶ ἄρκος
lines.en: of wine and a zamara and horns of a gazelle-antelope and a duck and a bear

lines.text: ἡπλωμένας ἔχουσα τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ
lines.en: having its hands spread out and the half of the Ship and the half

lines.text: τοῦ ὄφεως τοῦ ὑδατώδους καὶ μέλανος καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ ἵππου καὶ τὸ
lines.en: of the watery and black snake and the half of the Horse and the

lines.text: ἥμισυ τοῦ ὄνου.
lines.en: half of the Ass.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Ἰνδοὺς παρανατέλλει ἀνὴρ λεπτός, ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς
lines.en: And according to the Indians there co-rises a thin man, having on his head

lines.text: αὐτοῦ στέφανον λευκὸν συντεθειμένον ἀπὸ φυτῶν εὐωδῶν, ἔχων ἐπὶ
lines.en: a white crown composed of fragrant plants, having in

lines.text: τῆς χειρὸς αὑτοῦ τόξον, ἔριδας ἔχων μετὰ κλεπτῶν, πονηρός, θυμώδης,
lines.en: his hand a bow, having quarrels with thieves, wicked, wrathful,

lines.text: καὶ ὅτε θυμώδης, ὅμοιος γίνεται λέοντι.
lines.en: and when wrathful, he becomes like a lion.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Πτολεμαῖον παρανατέλλει ὁ ὦμος τῆς μεγάλης ἄρκτου καὶ
lines.en: And according to Ptolemy there co-rises the shoulder of the Great Bear and

lines.text: ὁ δεξιὸς αὐτῆς ποὺς καὶ ὁ τράχηλος τοῦ Λέοντος καὶ τὰ μέσα τοῦ
lines.en: its right foot and the neck of Leo and the middle parts of

lines.text: Ὠρίωνος.
lines.en: Orion.

lines.text: Τῷ δὲ γʹ δεκανῷ τοῦ Λέοντος παρανατέλλει ἀνὴρ νέος ἱπποκρά-
lines.en: And with the 3rd decan of Leo there co-rises a young man, a horse-

lines.text: τωρ κατέχων μαγκλάβια ἐν τῇ χειρί, ἔχων ἅμαξαν, ἐφ’ ἧς ἐπιβαίνουσι
lines.en: master, holding whips in his hand, having a wagon, on which mount

lines.text: ἄνθρωπος καὶ παῖς· παρανατέλλει δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ κόραξ καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ
lines.en: a man and a boy; and there co-rises with him also a raven and the half

lines.text: τοῦ ὄφεως τοῦ μέλανος καὶ ὑδατώδους καὶ τὰ ὀπίσθια τοῦ τε ἵππου
lines.en: of the black and watery snake and the hind parts of both the Horse

lines.text: καὶ τοῦ ὄνου.
lines.en: and the Ass.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Ἰνδοὺς παρανατέλλει ἀνὴρ ἔχων τὸ εἶδος τῶν ζιγγῶν,
lines.en: And according to the Indians there co-rises a man having the appearance of the Zings,

lines.text: ἀσχημοπρόσωπος, πολύκοπος, πολυφρόντιστος, τρώγων ὀπώρας καὶ
lines.en: ugly-faced, much-toiling, full of cares, eating fruits and

lines.text: κρέας, κατέχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὑτοῦ ξέστα.
lines.en: meat, holding in his hand a sextarius-measure.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Πτολεμαῖον παρανατέλλει τὸ στῆθος τῆς μεγάλης ἄρκτου
lines.en: And according to Ptolemy there co-rises the breast of the Great Bear

lines.text: καὶ τὸ βʹ ἥμισυ τοῦ Λέοντος καὶ μέρος τι τοῦ Ὠρίωνος.
lines.en: and the 2nd half of Leo and a certain part of Orion.

lines.text: Τῆς δὲ Παρθένου τῷ αʹ δεκανῷ παρανατέλλει γυνὴ γραῖς παρθέ-
lines.en: And with the 1st decan of Virgo there co-rises an old virgin woman,

lines.text: νος καθαρωτάτη, μακρόθριξ, ὡραία, κατέχουσα ἐν τῇ χειρὶ δύο ἀστά-
lines.en: very pure, long-haired, beautiful, holding in her hand two ears of corn

sections.text: 4 παῖς : “ deus „ Arab. Interpres Graecus legit “ ṣabijj „ (Dyroff). 6 ὀρχηστήν : “ cymbala qualia saltatores habent „ Arab. 6 τραγωδή cod. 7 ζαμάρα : cf. supra p. 159, 33. δορκάδες cod. ἄρκος frequenter pro ἄρκτος, cf. Crönert, Mem. Gr. Herculan., p. 87, 1. 8 ἡπλωμένας : “ brachiis ad caelum porrectis „ Arab. ; cf. neogr. ἁπλόνω. 11 λεπτός debebat esse nasus huius hominis. In textu Arabico signum corruptelae delendum et vocabulum alriqqa suis signis diacriticis instituendum est ; in translatione scribas “ ein Mann mit ziemlich dünner Nase „ ; Achmes, Catal., II, p. 154, 32 : ῥὶς αὐτοῦ οἷον σινάπεως vel συνάπεως : Dyroff coniecit σπάνιος. Nunc a Varahamihira genuinam lectionem discimus (p. 370, num. 14) : “ vir insignis naso adunco „. 18 ἱπποκράτωρ scripsi, cf. Sphaera, p. 282 : ἱπποκράτης cod. ; eadem corruptela in Excerpto Barocciano altero, Sphaera, p. 466, 7. 19 μεγηλά- βια cod. ; correxi : “ flagellum „ Arab. 23 ζιγγῶν cod. : Arab. al-Zing i. e. “ nigritae „, Zingitae unde nomen Zanzibar ; “ simiae similis „ Varahamihira ; “ nigritae similis „ Apomasar Arab. 24 πολυφρό cod. 25 ξέστον = “ aquimanile „ Du Cange : “ Giesskanne „ vertit Dyroff ex Arab. 28 γραῖς i. e. gārija “ puella „ textus Arabici (Dyroff).
sections.en: 4 παῖς ('child') : "god" Arabic. The Greek translator read "ṣabijj" (Dyroff). 6 ὀρχηστήν ('dancer') : "cymbals such as dancers have" Arabic. 6 τραγωδή ('tragic actress') the codex has. 7 ζαμάρα ('flute') : compare above p. 159, 33. δορκάδες ('gazelles') the codex has. ἄρκος ('bear') frequently for ἄρκτος ('bear'), compare Crönert, Mem. Gr. Herculan., p. 87, 1. 8 ἡπλωμένας ('spread out') : "with arms stretched out to the sky" Arabic ; compare Modern Greek ἁπλόνω ('I spread'). 11 λεπτός ('thin') ought to be the nose of this man. In the Arabic text the sign of corruption must be deleted and the word alriqqa must be established with its diacritic signs ; in the translation you should write "a man with a rather thin nose" ; Achmes, Catal., II, p. 154, 32 : ῥὶς αὐτοῦ οἷον σινάπεως ('his nose like mustard') or συνάπεως ('mustard') : Dyroff conjectured σπάνιος ('rare'). Now from Varahamihira we learn the genuine reading (p. 370, num. 14) : "a man distinguished by a hooked nose". 18 ἱπποκράτωρ ('horse-master') I have written, compare Sphaera, p. 282 : ἱπποκράτης ('Hippocrates') the codex has ; the same corruption in the second Baroccian Excerpt, Sphaera, p. 466, 7. 19 μεγηλά- βια ('whips') the codex has ; I have corrected : "whip" Arabic. 23 ζιγγῶν ('of the Zanj') the codex has : Arabic al-Zing that is "black people", Zingitae whence the name Zanzibar ; "similar to a monkey" Varahamihira ; "similar to a black person" Apomasar Arabic. 24 πολυφρό ('very wise') the codex has. 25 ξέστον ('pitcher') = "washbasin" Du Cange : "watering can" translates Dyroff from Arabic. 28 γραῖς ('old woman') that is gārija "girl" of the Arabic text (Dyroff).

summary.headline: Leo and Virgo Decan Figures
summary.text: Astrological descriptions of the second and third decans of Leo and the first decan of Virgo, comparing Ptolemy’s co-rising constellations with Indian figures and associated animals, objects, and stars. The notes discuss Arabic and Greek readings with references to Varahamihira, Achmes, Apomasar, Dyroff, Crönert, and Du Cange.
